project.name: strata-mcp
project.description: Local memory layer for AI agents — coding assistants over MCP, game NPCs over REST. SQLite/D1/Postgres storage with BM25+vector+RRF hybrid search and quality-gated extraction pipeline.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes node_modules, build artifacts, tests, and dev files from the Docker build context to keep image layers small and reproducible.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Node.js 22 Alpine build: a builder stage compiles TypeScript via npm run build, then a slim runtime stage copies dist/ and node_modules, runs as the non-root strata user, exposes port 8080, and launches the MCP server via dist/cli.js serve.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build pattern separates compile-time deps (python3/make/g++ for native modules like better-sqlite3) from the runtime image, which only carries libstdc++ alongside the compiled output. HEALTHCHECK is configured for orchestrator liveness.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Single-service Docker Compose definition that builds the Strata image, maps host port 3000 to container 8080, mounts a named volume for /data persistence, and forwards STRATA_LICENSE_KEY for Pro tier activation.

nodes.name: aws-template-apply.yml
nodes.summary: Manually-triggered GitHub Actions workflow that applies (or destroys) the AWS dev environment Terraform stack via `task dev:up`/`dev:down` using OIDC-federated deploy role assumption.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses OIDC federation (id-token: write) to assume a deploy role without long-lived AWS credentials, and pins all actions to SHA digests for supply chain hardening.

nodes.name: aws-template-ci.yml
nodes.summary: Pull-request CI pipeline for AWS Terraform templates running fmt, validate, tflint, checkov, tfsec, and plan-on-PR jobs via dynamic matrix path discovery.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a discover job to dynamically build a Terraform path matrix from versions.tf locations, then fans out validation jobs across each path.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Main pull-request and push CI workflow running build, tests, security audit, and license compliance checks for the strata-mcp package.

nodes.name: publish.yml
nodes.summary: Tag-triggered workflow that publishes strata-mcp to npm when a `v*` git tag is pushed.

nodes.name: security.yml
nodes.summary: Security scanning pipeline running Semgrep SAST, Gitleaks secret detection, and npm audit on pull requests with a gate job and PR comment summary.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Single job that gates on a confirmation string, configures OIDC AWS credentials, runs `task dev:up` (or `dev:down`), and uploads orchestrator outputs as an artifact.

nodes.name: discover
nodes.summary: Discovers all Terraform module paths under templates/aws by searching for versions.tf files and emits a JSON matrix for downstream fan-out.

nodes.name: fmt
nodes.summary: Runs `terraform fmt -check -recursive` across the entire templates/aws tree to enforce formatting consistency.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Per-path terraform validate job with backend disabled, fanned out across the discovered Terraform module matrix.

nodes.name: tflint
nodes.summary: Runs tflint static analysis on each discovered Terraform module to surface style and provider issues.

nodes.name: checkov
nodes.summary: Runs Checkov IaC security/compliance scanning against each Terraform module for misconfiguration detection.

nodes.name: tfsec
nodes.summary: Runs tfsec security analysis against Terraform modules to detect known security issues in infrastructure code.

nodes.name: plan-on-pr
nodes.summary: Runs `terraform plan` on pull requests to surface the proposed infrastructure diff before merge.

nodes.name: build-and-test
nodes.summary: Installs dependencies, builds TypeScript, and runs the strata test suite on every PR and push to main.

nodes.name: security-audit
nodes.summary: Runs npm audit and Semgrep static analysis to surface dependency vulnerabilities and code-level security issues.

nodes.name: license-check
nodes.summary: Validates dependency licenses to ensure no incompatible licenses are introduced into the project.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: Builds the package and runs `npm publish` to release strata-mcp to the npm registry on version tag push.

nodes.name: semgrep
nodes.summary: Runs Semgrep SAST scan using custom rules from .semgrep/custom-rules.yml to detect secrets, injection, and prototype pollution issues.

nodes.name: gitleaks
nodes.summary: Runs Gitleaks scan against the repository to detect leaked credentials and secrets in commits.

nodes.name: npm-audit
nodes.summary: Runs npm audit to surface vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies of the strata-mcp package.

nodes.name: security-gate
nodes.summary: Aggregates results from Semgrep, Gitleaks, and npm audit and fails the workflow if any ERROR-severity finding blocks the PR.

nodes.name: pr-comment
nodes.summary: Posts a summary comment on the pull request with security scan findings from all upstream jobs.

nodes.name: 0001_init.sql
nodes.summary: Initial D1/SQLite schema migration creating the full core data model: conversation documents, extracted knowledge entries with history, session summaries, embeddings, entity graph, evidence gaps, and analytics — plus supporting indexes.

nodes.name: 0002_quantization_support.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the migration_state table and quantization-related columns to embeddings to support int8/binary vector quantization rollouts.

nodes.name: 0003_knowledge_fts.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the knowledge_fts FTS5 virtual table with porter stemming plus insert/delete/update sync triggers, replacing the slow LIKE-based knowledge search that did not scale past a few thousand entries under D1's 30s CPU limit.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FTS5 contentless-rowid pattern (content=knowledge) so the index references the base table rather than duplicating storage; trigger pattern is the standard 'insert delete' command idiom for external-content FTS5 tables.

nodes.name: 0004_knowledge_turns.sql
nodes.summary: Introduces the knowledge_turns table for storing verbatim conversation turns linked to extracted knowledge entries, supporting the turn-level retrieval adapter design.

nodes.name: 0001_baseline.sql
nodes.summary: Postgres baseline migration that creates the entire Strata schema for Tier B deployments — 16 tables covering conversation documents, extracted knowledge, summaries, entities, events, evidence gaps, analytics, vector embeddings, stored documents/chunks, and Phase 0 training data capture, plus all supporting indexes including tsvector FTS indexes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Postgres tsvector columns for FTS (parallels the SQLite FTS5 virtual tables used in single-user mode). Includes embedding bytea columns for vector search and a migration_state table to track vector quantization bit-width transitions.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start at the README to understand what Strata is: a local memory layer for AI coding assistants that auto-indexes Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Cline, and Gemini CLI conversations into a SQLite/FTS5 database and exposes 15 MCP tools for search and recall. The README sketches the three transport modes (stdio, HTTP single- and multi-tenant), the three storage backends (SQLite, Cloudflare D1, Postgres on GCP), and Strata's flagship 81.1% LongMemEval-500 result driven by BM25 + vector + RRF hybrid retrieval. Treat this step as the map you will follow through the rest of the codebase.

tour.title: Entry Points: CLI and stdio Server
tour.description: Strata exposes two thin top-level entry points. `src/index.ts` is the stdio entry — invoked when an MCP client like Claude Code spawns `strata` — and it just constructs the MCP server and wires it to the stdio transport. `src/cli.ts` is the umbrella CLI that parses arguments and dispatches to subcommands (`serve`, `distill`, `init`, `deploy`, `backup`, etc.). These files are deliberately minimal: the real work happens in the server factory you will visit next.

tour.title: The Server Factory — Where Everything Is Wired
tour.description: `src/server.ts` is the heart of the runtime. Its `createServer()` factory is what every transport (stdio, HTTP, multi-tenant, REST) ultimately calls to build a fully-configured MCP server instance. It opens the database, constructs the IndexManager, storage layer, search engine, and registers all MCP tool handlers — and it accepts a `{ dataDir }` override so the multi-tenant transport can give each user an isolated server instance with their own database and caches. Because downstream packages (`strata-pro`, `strata-team`) import this factory, its signature is a load-bearing contract.

tour.title: MCP Tool Handlers — The User-Facing API
tour.description: The 15 MCP tools registered by the server live in `src/tools/`. `search_history` is the flagship retrieval entry point that routes between FTS5, vector, and hybrid backends; `store_memory` persists a structured knowledge entry (decision, error_fix, learning) and is what `/remember` invokes; `find_solutions` searches knowledge for prior fixes to an error — the read side of the loop that makes Strata learn from itself. Together these handlers are the public API that AI agents call; everything downstream exists to make their answers fast and high-quality.

tour.title: The Search Engine — BM25 + Vector + RRF
tour.description: When `search_history` runs, it delegates to the `SearchEngine` wrapper, which in turn drives the SQLite search implementation. `sqlite-search-engine.ts` is the primary backend: it combines BM25/FTS5 lexical retrieval, vector similarity over stored embeddings, and reciprocal-rank fusion (RRF) of the two lanes, then applies `result-ranker.ts` for recency, project, and speaker boosts. This is the pipeline whose AutoResearch-optimized parameters (`rrfK=40`, `bm25.k1=1.2`, etc., locked in `src/config.ts`) produce the 81.1% LongMemEval result.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines two ranked lists by summing `1 / (k + rank)` per document across lanes, where `k` (here 40) damps the contribution of low-ranked items. It is parameter-light, requires no score normalization across lanes, and is robust to lexical/semantic score scales being incomparable — which is why it is the default fusion strategy in modern hybrid search.

tour.title: Indexing — From Raw Text to BM25 + FTS5
tour.description: Before search can work, conversation logs must be parsed, tokenized, and indexed. `indexing/sqlite-index-manager.ts` orchestrates multi-parser discovery and FTS5 indexing; `indexing/bm25.ts` is a pure-JS BM25 inverted index used for the lexical channel; `parsers/parser-registry.ts` selects the right parser per session-log format, and `parsers/claude-code-parser.ts` is the canonical example — it walks `~/.claude/projects/`, parses JSONL transcripts turn by turn, and feeds them into the indexer. Strata's tagline of "automatic" memory comes from this layer running quietly in the background.

tour.title: Storage Layer — One Interface, Three Backends
tour.description: The storage factory (`src/storage/factory.ts`) selects between SQLite (default, local), Cloudflare D1 (edge), and Postgres (GCP Cloud SQL) at runtime. Every backend implements the same interface contracts in `src/storage/interfaces/`, so the server doesn't care which one is mounted. `database.ts` handles the local SQLite case (better-sqlite3 + path resolution + WAL), while `sqlite-knowledge-store.ts` is the canonical reference implementation of `IKnowledgeStore`: CRUD, edit history, hybrid FTS5+LIKE search, and async embedding generation. The D1 and Postgres barrels (`d1/index.ts`, `pg/index.ts`) wire equivalent adapter families for their respective platforms.

tour.title: The Quality-Gated Knowledge Pipeline
tour.description: Not every assistant utterance is worth remembering. Before a candidate knowledge entry is stored, it passes through a quality gate: `knowledge-extractor.ts` mines candidates from messages (decisions, error fixes, learnings, patterns); `knowledge-evaluator.ts` scores each candidate on **actionability**, **specificity**, and **relevance** and rejects low-scoring ones; `conflict-resolver.ts` then uses an LLM to merge or supersede semantically conflicting entries already in the store. This pipeline is why Strata's memory stays useful instead of accumulating noise — and it's the layer that distinguishes it from naive vector-dump approaches.

tour.title: LLM Extension Layer — Pluggable Providers + Local Distillation
tour.description: All LLM-driven work in Strata (extraction, summarization, conflict resolution, semantic embeddings) goes through a pluggable provider interface. `llm-extraction/llm-provider.ts` defines the `LlmProvider` contract and ships the `OllamaProvider` for local Gemma 4; `hybrid-provider.ts` is the local-first wrapper that tries Ollama first and falls back to Gemini on failure; `provider-factory.ts` picks the right provider per stage based on `~/.strata/config.json`. The `extensions/embeddings/gemini-embedder.ts` is the production vector encoder for community-tier semantic search, called by the indexer to populate the embedding column the search engine then ranks against.
tour.languageLesson: The provider-factory pattern (a function that returns one of several implementations of a shared interface based on runtime configuration) is how Strata stays vendor-neutral. New providers only need to satisfy `LlmProvider`; the rest of the codebase imports the interface, never the concrete class. This is what makes `strata distill activate` a single config flip rather than a refactor.

tour.title: Transports — stdio, HTTP, Multi-Tenant, REST/NPC
tour.description: Strata's transport layer is where the same MCP server gets reused across deployment models. `http-transport.ts` is the single-tenant Streamable HTTP transport (one user, one DB). `multi-tenant-http-transport.ts` is the SaaS model — one Node process, an LRU pool of per-user SQLite databases keyed by the `X-Strata-User` header, with the `X-Strata-Verified` sentinel enforcing that an upstream auth proxy has validated the caller. `npc-memory-engine.ts` and `player-token.ts` are the REST-transport NPC pieces: per-NPC memory plus HMAC-signed player bearer tokens for Unity/Godot/Unreal game integrations. Each transport calls back into the same `createServer()` factory from Step 3.

tour.title: Database Schemas and Deployment
tour.description: The D1 baseline migration (`0001_init.sql`) is the cleanest single-file picture of Strata's data model: `knowledge`, `entities`, `entity_relations`, `knowledge_entities` (the junction graph), `documents`, `summaries`, `embeddings`, `evidence_gaps`, and `analytics`. The same schema is bootstrapped in SQLite and Postgres by the storage layer you saw in Step 7. The `Dockerfile` packages the multi-tenant HTTP server for container deployment, and the CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs build, tests, npm audit, and license checks on every PR, gating what gets published to npm.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations are intentionally forward-only and immutable: once `0001_init.sql` ships, you never edit it — you add `0002_*.sql`. Each backend (SQLite, D1, Postgres) keeps its own migration folder so platform-specific syntax (e.g. PG `tsvector`, D1's lack of `STRICT`) can diverge without breaking the shared interface contract.

tour.title: Evals — Where Quality Claims Come From
tour.description: Strata's headline numbers (81.1% LongMemEval-500, the AutoResearch ceilings in `src/config.ts`) are not marketing — they are reproducible eval runs. `evals/distillation-e2e/run-eval.ts` is a representative example: it drives the full pipeline (extraction → storage → retrieval → scoring) against a frozen scenario set and reports recall, precision, and judge scores. The frozen-eval discipline (eval script never modified during optimization, one variable changed per iteration) is what lets contributors safely tune the 34 parameters in `src/config.ts` without regressing the benchmark. If you change anything in the search, indexing, or knowledge layers, this is the test bench you run before opening a PR.
